cues.say: Component 20: Load test and game day. A load test fires fake traffic at 2 to 3 times the peak at a test copy, with a pass bar. A game day rehearses: flip switches, fake outages. You'll bring this up during go-live prep.
Think of it as: A dress rehearsal before opening night. Use it for before every launch.
Here's a real scenario. Two days before a doorbuster sale.
Without it: A missing index is found at 6 AM on sale day.
On-call has never practiced pausing orders.
With it: k6 simulates 120,000 visitors, 1,000 buying one TV.
Pass bar: 50 sold per deal, 0 double charges, p ninety-five under 800 milliseconds.
Run 1 fails (missing index); fix, rerun, pass.
Game day: flip every switch, fake Stripe errors, time the response.
Why it works: You find the missing index on Tuesday, not at 6 AM on Friday.
In the interview, say: Pass means 0 oversold, 0 double charges, and p ninety-five under 500 milliseconds.
A few related terms you may hear.
Staging: The test copy of your system.
Chaos testing: Breaking parts on purpose. Game day is the small version.
Capacity planning: Your Clarify math, written down.
